name: SCHOOL_BUS_ROUTE_YELLOW_DIAMOND

tas_w6-101_bus_child.desc: front of a bus with a child (schoolgirl with a bag) walking at its right, traced from the sheet (black graphics); the same artwork at a smaller size on W6-102 (G/10/445A)

notes: Department of State Growth (formerly DIER) standard drawing, black line-work sheet; every dimension from the sheet unless stated. Series/heights as the sheet's letter-type note; AS 1744 (plus0) spacing, so widths differ from the sheet's figures where its spacing is wider (the TAS sheets' 'medium'/'75%' spacing runs about 7% wider than AS 1744 normal spacing). Sheet G/10/445A 'General school bus route sign W6-102' (1998, sideways A4): sizes A 600 to D 1200, drawn at A (600, bounding square 848.53); 'lettering 50mm high with gap between rows 40mm, black lettering & graphics on yellow background'; no border drawn (none generated), R40 as the AS 1743 600 diamonds. Letter series not stated: Series D fits the drawn widths within 4% (SCHOOL 264 / BUS 123 / ROUTE 207 measured; D: 255 / 119 / 199). Positions measured on the sheet (no scale given, the drawn diamond taken as the 600 sign): symbol 346 x 325 at (306, 168), SCHOOL BUS cap top 558 with a 41 word gap, ROUTE top 639 (40 row gap), both centred. Symbol reused from W6-101 (same artwork). panel_px = the sheet's diamond extent widened by the tip rounding (R40: 16.6 each side) to the sharp bounding square.
